title: Laser Cutting Design and Toolpath Program — Overview and definition
t: Laser Cutting Design and Toolpath Program — Overview and definition
description: Lays out flat patterns and generates laser cut/engrave toolpaths with kerf compensation.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Lays out flat patterns and generates laser cut/engrave toolpaths with kerf compensation. A laser cutting program imports vector designs, nests parts on sheet stock, applies kerf compensation and lead-in/out, and orders cut sequences to minimize heat distortion. Real implementations include LightBurn, RDWorks, and Glowforge's cloud software. It separates cut, score, and engrave layers by power/speed settings and simulates the job time.
capabilities: Vector import with automatic nesting on sheet sizes
Kerf compensation and tab/bridge placement
Layer-based power/speed/frequency recipes per material
Cut sequencing to control heat and part tipping
Camera alignment and job time estimation

Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Vector import with automatic nesting on sheet sizes). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output.
